residential_re_roofing_roof_repairs.text: id="main" class="site-main"> RESIDENTIAL RE-ROOFING & ROOF REPAIRS Residential Re-Roofing & Roof Repairs Your roof is one of the most important components of your home, providing protection from the elements and ensuring your family’s safety and comfort. Over time, however, wear and tear can take a toll, leading to the need for roof repairs or even a full re-roofing. At S&S Roofing, we specialize in both residential re-roofing and roof repairs , offering reliable and affordable solutions to keep your home safe, dry, and secure. Call us today at +801-272-7000 Residential Re-Roofing: A New Roof for Your Home If your roof is showing signs of significant damage or wear, it may be time to consider a complete re-roofing. The process involves the installation of a new roof over your existing one, a cost-effective and efficient solution to restore the integrity of your home’s roofing system. Why Choose Re-Roofing? Cost-Effective Solution: Re-roofing is often less expensive than a complete roof replacement, as it involves placing new shingles or materials over the old roof. Faster Installation: This solution can typically be completed faster than a full replacement, minimizing disruption to your daily life. Improved Curb Appeal: A new roof will enhance the appearance of your home, increasing its value and aesthetic appeal. Long-Lasting Protection: With a fresh layer of roofing, your home will be protected from leaks, storm damage, and other common roofing issues. Signs You Need a Re-Roofing: Multiple layers of shingles that are difficult to repair. Significant wear, curling, or cracking of existing shingles. Severe weather damage or aging roof. Frequent leaks or water damage inside your home Our Process Initial Assessment: We begin with a thorough inspection of your roof to evaluate its current condition and determine whether it’s the best option for you. Material Selection: We offer a wide range of high-quality roofing materials, including asphalt shingles, metal roofing, and more. Our team will help you choose the best material to suit your home’s style and your budget. Installation: Our experienced team will install your new roof with precision and care, ensuring your home is fully protected. Final Inspection: After installation, we perform a detailed inspection to ensure the roof is properly installed and meets our high-quality standards. Prevent Further Damage: Addressing issues early can prevent the need for a full re-roofing and save you money in the long run. Extend Roof Life: Regular roof repairs can extend the life of your roof, ensuring it remains functional for years to come. Quick Turnaround: Roof repairs are generally completed quickly, minimizing disruption to your home. Common Roof Repair Issues: Leaking Roofs: Leaks can occur due to damaged shingles, broken flashing, or clogged gutters. They can lead to water damage inside your home if left untreated. Damaged Shingles: Missing or broken shingles can expose your home to the elements, causing further damage. Storm Damage: Hail, high winds, and heavy rain can damage your roof, requiring repairs to restore its protective function. Sagging Roofs: A sagging roof can be a sign of structural issues that require immediate attention. Our Process Inspection: We begin by assessing the damage to your roof. how_your_roof_protects_your_entire_home_.text: id="main" class="site-main"> HOW YOUR ROOF PROTECTS YOUR ENTIRE HOME & WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN YOU THINK How Your Roof Protects Your Entire Home & Why It Matters More Than You Think When most homeowners think about their roof, they picture shingles and curb appeal. But your roof is doing far more than looking good, it’s quietly protecting every single part of your home, day and night, in every season. At S & S Roofing, Inc. , we like to say your roof is your home’s first and most important line of defense . Here’s how it works behind the scenes and why a healthy roof is essential to everything underneath it. Get in Touch! Your Home’s Built-In Shield Against the Elements Your roof is an all-encompassing protective system designed to handle whatever nature throws at it. Shingles, underlayment, flashing, and ventilation all work together like a team. Sun protection: The outer roofing surface reflects and repels harmful UV rays, reducing long-term damage to siding, windows, and exterior finishes. Water defense: Rain, snow, and melting ice are sealed out before they ever reach your attic or walls. Moisture control: A properly installed roof prevents water intrusion that can cause wood rot, mold growth, insulation failure, and even pest infestations. When a roof fails, the damage rarely stays on the roof. It spreads through walls, ceilings, and structural components quickly and expensively. Protecting What You Can’t See: Structure & Foundation Your roof doesn’t just protect what’s above. It safeguards what’s below. A complete roofing system directs water away from your home’s perimeter , using gutters and downspouts to prevent: Soil erosion around the foundation Water saturation that can cause foundation cracks or shifting Damage to landscaping and walkways Additionally, the roof deck plays a key structural role by distributing weight evenly across the home. This helps your house withstand: Heavy snow loads High winds Seasonal stress and movement Without a solid roof system, the entire structure becomes more vulnerable. Comfort, Energy Efficiency & Lower Utility Bills A great roof doesn’t just keep water out — it keeps comfort in. Proper attic ventilation and insulation, designed as part of the roofing system, help regulate indoor temperatures by: Reflecting heat during hot summer months Trapping warmth inside during winter Reducing strain on HVAC systems The payoff? – More consistent indoor temperatures – Fewer drafts and hot/cold spots – Lower heating and cooling costs – A more comfortable home year-round If your home feels harder to heat or cool, your roof may be the hidden culprit. The Takeaway: Your Roof Protects Everything Your roof isn’t just a layer on top of your home, it’s a protective system that shields your structure, foundation, comfort, and investment. When it’s properly installed and maintained, it quietly does its job for decades. When it’s compromised, the consequences ripple through the entire house. That’s why at S & S Roofing, Inc. , we believe quality roofing is about more than materials. It’s about protecting what matters most underneath. If you’re unsure about the condition of your roof or want peace of mind as the seasons change, our team is always here to help. what_is_a_roofing_cricket_why_are_they_n.text: id="main" class="site-main"> WHAT IS A ROOFING CRICKET? WHY ARE THEY NEEDED? What is a Roofing Cricket? A roof cricket, also known as a saddle, is a triangular-shaped structure designed to divert water and debris away from vertical protrusions on a roof surface, such as chimneys, skylights, or HVAC units. Its main purpose is to prevent water from pooling at the base of these obstacles, which can lead to leaks, wood rot, mold, and damage to the roof structure and flashing over time. Crickets act as a “water traffic cop” to ensure continuous water flow towards drains or gutters, thus extending the lifespan of the entire roofing system. Roof Crickets for Flat Roofs and TPO Membrane Systems For TPO (thermoplastic polyolefin) or other low-sloped and flat roofs, crickets are designed and installed differently but serve the same primary function of ensuring positive drainage. Instead of wood framing, they are typically constructed using tapered rigid insulation panels that are laid on top of the roof deck and then covered entirely with the TPO membrane to create a continuous, watertight seal. These crickets often have a steeper slope than the main roof to actively force water towards drains or scuppers and prevent ponding, which is a major cause of membrane failure on flat roofs. Their shape can be a full diamond pattern (between two drains) or a quarter diamond (in a corner by a parapet wall). Chimney Roof Crickets for Shingle and Steep-Slope Roofs On shingled, or steep-sloped, roofs, crickets are typically custom-built with wood framing and sheathing, then covered with the same asphalt shingles or durable metal flashing used on the rest of the roof to create a seamless appearance. They are most commonly installed on the high (upslope) side of chimneys, especially if the chimney is wider than 30 inches, as this is where water and snowmelt naturally accumulate. The cricket’s pitch (slope) is usually the same as or slightly less than the main roof’s slope and serves to split the flow of water and direct it around the sides of the obstruction and down the roof to the gutters. why_proper_roof_drains_matter_for_flat_r.text: id="main" class="site-main"> WHY PROPER ROOF DRAINS MATTER FOR FLAT ROOFING SYSTEMS Why Proper Roof Drains Matter for Flat Roofing Systems When it comes to flat and low-slope roofing, drainage is everything . Unlike pitched roofs that naturally shed water, flat roofs rely on a carefully designed drainage system to move water safely off the surface. Without proper drains, standing water (also known as ponding) can lead to leaks, structural damage, and premature roof failure. At S & S Roofing , we install high-performance drainage solutions designed to protect your building, extend the life of your roof, and prevent costly repairs. One of the most effective options we use for TPO roofing systems is the OlyFlow Hercules Drain . Why Roof Drains Are So Important Flat roofs are constantly exposed to rain, snowmelt, and debris. Built for Durability & Performance OlyFlow Hercules drains are made from: One-piece spun aluminum body Heavy-duty cast aluminum strainer and clamping ring Corrosion-resistant materials They’re designed to last and withstand harsh weather conditions without rusting or deteriorating. The depressed sump design also helps water flow efficiently toward the drain, preventing ponding water that adds unnecessary weight and stress to the roof structure. Faster Drainage with Vortex Breaker Technology Hercules-Plus models include an integrated vortex breaker , which can increase drainage capacity by up to 2.5 times compared to standard drains.
